title: A filtering method to reveal crystalline patterns from atom probe microscopy desorption maps
author: Yao

steps.title: Prepare needle‑shaped specimen
steps.instruction: Use focused ion beam milling (e.g., FEI Helios) to shape the sample into a needle with a tip radius of 20–100 nm; for this protocol use Fe‑15 at.% Cr alloy.

steps.title: Configure atom probe instrument
steps.instruction: Mount the specimen in a Cameca LEAP 4000XHR, cool to 50 K, set voltage‑pulse repetition rate to 200 kHz and pulse fraction to 20 %.

steps.title: Collect desorption data
steps.instruction: Run the APM experiment, recording for each detected ion the number of voltage (or laser) pulses Np elapsed since the previous evaporation event.

steps.title: Generate Np histogram
steps.instruction: Export the Np values for all ions and plot a histogram; the distribution should show an exponential decay with a deviation at low Np, indicating non‑random evaporation.

steps.title: Filter low‑Np events
steps.instruction: Select only ions with Np < 10 pulses; discard all events with Np ≥ 10.

steps.title: Create filtered desorption map
steps.instruction: Using the filtered ion list, reconstruct a 2‑D desorption map; the resulting map should display enhanced crystalline patterns (e.g., visible [001] pole).

steps.title: Analyze crystallographic patterns
steps.instruction: Identify poles, zone lines, and symmetry in the filtered map to determine crystal orientation; for specimens containing grain boundaries, repeat the analysis for each grain.
